verses: وَأَمَّا عَادٌ فَأُهْلِكُوا۟ بِرِيحٍ صَرْصَرٍ عَاتِيَةٍ
سَخَّرَهَا عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ لَيَالٍ وَثَمَٰنِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُومًا فَتَرَى ٱلْقَوْمَ فِيهَا صَرْعَىٰ كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ
وَجَآءَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَن قَبْلَهُۥ وَٱلْمُؤْتَفِكَٰتُ بِٱلْخَاطِئَةِ
فَعَصَوْا۟ رَسُولَ رَبِّهِمْ فَأَخَذَهُمْ أَخْذَةً رَّابِيَةً
إِنَّا لَمَّا طَغَا ٱلْمَآءُ حَمَلْنَٰكُمْ فِى ٱلْجَارِيَةِ
لِنَجْعَلَهَا لَكُمْ تَذْكِرَةً وَتَعِيَهَآ أُذُنٌ وَٰعِيَةٌ
فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِى ٱلصُّورِ نَفْخَةٌ وَٰحِدَةٌ
وَحُمِلَتِ ٱلْأَرْضُ وَٱلْجِبَالُ فَدُكَّتَا دَكَّةً وَٰحِدَةً
وَٱلْمَلَكُ عَلَىٰٓ أَرْجَآئِهَا وَيَحْمِلُ عَرْشَ رَبِّكَ فَوْقَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ ثَمَٰنِيَةٌ
يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ لَا تَخْفَىٰ مِنكُمْ خَافِيَةٌ
فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِىَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِيَمِينِهِۦ فَيَقُولُ هَآؤُمُ ٱقْرَءُوا۟ كِتَٰبِيَهْ
كُلُوا۟ وَٱشْرَبُوا۟ هَنِيٓـًٔۢا بِمَآ أَسْلَفْتُمْ فِى ٱلْأَيَّامِ ٱلْخَالِيَةِ
وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِىَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِشِمَالِهِۦ فَيَقُولُ يَٰلَيْتَنِى لَمْ أُوتَ كِتَٰبِيَهْ
ثُمَّ فِى سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُهَا سَبْعُونَ ذِرَاعًا فَٱسْلُكُوهُ
إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
وَمَا هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شَاعِرٍ قَلِيلًا مَّا تُؤْمِنُونَ
وَلَا بِقَوْلِ كَاهِنٍ قَلِيلًا مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ
فَمَا مِنكُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حَٰجِزِينَ

leads.title: Psalm 69, the waters have come up to my neck; gall and vinegar ↔ The book in the right hand and in the left, the seventy-cubit chain, ghislin, and the aorta of a forger
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God keeps a book in which names are written and from which sinners are blotted [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); God keeps a book in which names are written and from which sinners are blotted (weight 5.4). Pair score 13.2.

Only in Psalm 69, the waters have come up to my neck; gall and vinegar: Enemies give the sufferer poison (rosh, gall) for food and vinegar to drink; Curse that the enemy's encampment be desolate with no one dwelling in his tents; Curse that the enemies' table become a trap and snare; Prayer that the pit (be'er) not close its mouth over the sufferer; What God's heavenly book records: names or deeds [divergence between the texts]; Heaven, earth, seas and all that moves in them praise God; Speaker fasts and wears sackcloth and becomes a byword and the song of drunkards; The record of the wicked is in Sijjin, that of the righteous in 'Illiyyun, each an inscribed book (kitab marqum) witnessed by those brought near [divergence between the texts]; Zeal for God's house consumes the speaker; Sufferer sinks in deep mire and floodwaters up to the neck, the underworld deep; Prayer that God rebuild the walls of Jerusalem/Zion; Those who hate the speaker without cause (hinnam); and 4 more.

Only in The book in the right hand and in the left, the seventy-cubit chain, ghislin, and the aorta of a forger: Whoever is given his book in his left hand wishes he had never been given it and that death had been final; his wealth and power are gone; Whoever is given his book in his right hand says 'Here, read my book!' and lives a pleasing life in a lofty garden with fruit clusters near; He did not believe in God the Great and did not urge the feeding of the poor; The damned have no friend and no food except ghislin (foul washings/pus); Had he fabricated sayings against God, God would have seized him by the right hand and cut his aorta (watin); 'I swear by what you see and what you do not see'; 'Seize him, fetter him, roast him in hellfire, then thread him on a chain seventy cubits long'; 'This is the certain truth' (haqq al-yaqin); Reclining on couches lined with brocade, with the fruit of the gardens hanging near; 'Eat and drink with relish for what you used to do'; An offence concerning food is repaid with foul food and drink [divergence between the texts]; Kings bound with chains and nobles with fetters of iron to execute 'the judgment written'; and 7 more.

matches.note: The heavenly book becomes a personal book handed over: Ps 69:29 yimmāḥû mi-ssēfer ḥayyîm we-ʿim ṣaddîqîm ʾal yikkātēvû (one roll of the living, names blotted out).
